title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 2 Sensor 2
shortDescription: The PCM detected an out-of-range heater resistance value for the bank 2 downstream oxygen sensor.
fullDescription:
P0060 is set when the engine control module measures heater element resistance outside the expected range on bank 2 sensor 2. The heater helps the sensor reach operating temperature quickly so closed-loop fueling and catalyst monitoring can run.

A failed heater delays readiness monitors and can increase cold-start emissions. The code usually indicates a bad sensor, wiring issue, or blown heater fuse.
safetyImpact: No immediate driving hazard, but emissions and fuel trims on bank 2 may drift until the heater recovers.

fixSteps.title: Scan and confirm
fixSteps.instruction: Read freeze frame and verify the code is current.

fixSteps.title: Check heater fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the O2 heater fuse in the engine bay fuse box.

fixSteps.title: Measure heater resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the sensor and measure across heater pins; compare to spec (usually 2-20 ohms).

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If resistance is out of spec, replace the bank 2 sensor 2 HO2S.

faq.a: Yes, short term, but fix before emissions testing.

faq.q: Will this hurt my catalytic converter?
faq.a: Not typically; this is a post-cat sensor used for monitoring.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 3
shortDescription: Heater control circuit fault detected on bank 2 sensor 3.
fullDescription:
P0061 indicates the PCM cannot properly control the heater circuit for the third oxygen sensor on bank 2. This sensor is used on vehicles with multiple post-catalyst sensors.

Causes include open or shorted heater wiring, a failed heater element, or a PCM driver fault. Slow warm-up delays closed-loop operation.
safetyImpact: No safety risk; emissions and readiness affected.

fixSteps.title: Retrieve code
fixSteps.instruction: Verify with scan tool and note freeze frame.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check the harness from PCM to sensor for damage.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor if needed
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new HO2S if heater element is open.

faq.a: No, only on vehicles with triple O2 sensor setups.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 3
shortDescription: Heater control circuit voltage is too low on bank 2 sensor 3.
fullDescription:
P0062 is stored when the PCM sees low voltage on the heater control line for bank 2 sensor 3. A short to ground or an open driver is typical.

The post-catalyst O2 sensors confirm catalyst efficiency, so a failed heater can set additional codes over time.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Look for grounded wires and chafed insulation.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure heater resistance and compare to spec.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the HO2S if heater is bad.

faq.a: Chafing against the exhaust or body panels.

title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 3
shortDescription: Heater circuit voltage is too high on bank 2 sensor 3.
fullDescription:
P0063 is set when the PCM detects unexpectedly high voltage on the heater control line, indicating an open circuit or short to voltage.

This often traces back to a blown fuse or disconnected sensor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the HO2S connector and check for corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Measure voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Check heater supply voltage with key on.

fixSteps.title: Repair or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Repair wiring or install new sensor.

faq.q: Could a loose connector cause this?
faq.a: Yes, often the easiest fix to try first.

title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 2 Sensor 3
shortDescription: Heater element resistance out of range on bank 2 sensor 3.
fullDescription:
P0064 indicates heater element resistance has drifted beyond spec. This is usually an aging sensor or internal break in the heating wire.

Replacement of the oxygen sensor is the typical repair.

faq.q: How long do O2 sensors last?

title: Air Assisted Injector Control Range/Performance
shortDescription: Air-assisted fuel injector system performance fault.
fullDescription:
P0065 is set when the PCM notes the air-assisted injector system performance is outside expected range. This system supplements atomization at low RPM on some vehicles.

Causes include vacuum leaks, clogged air ports, or a stuck control valve.
safetyImpact: Rough idle possible, no safety risk.

fixSteps.title: Inspect vacuum lines
fixSteps.instruction: Check for cracked or disconnected hoses.

faq.a: No, only ones with air-assist injection.

title: Air Assisted Injector Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Low voltage in air-assisted injector control circuit.
fullDescription:
P0066 indicates a short to ground or open in the air-assist injector control circuit. The PCM cannot command the valve properly.

Inspect wiring and the control solenoid.

title: Air Assisted Injector Control Circuit High
shortDescription: High voltage in air-assisted injector control circuit.
fullDescription:
P0067 triggers when control circuit voltage is higher than expected, suggesting an open circuit or short to power.

Repair includes wiring inspection and solenoid testing.

title: MAP/MAF - Throttle Position Correlation
shortDescription: The PCM detected a mismatch between airflow/MAP and throttle position.
fullDescription:
P0068 is stored when intake airflow (MAF or MAP) does not match the expected value based on throttle position. This often indicates a vacuum leak, dirty MAF, or throttle body problem.

Drivability may suffer because fuel strategy relies on accurate airflow data.
safetyImpact: Reduced power or limp mode possible.

fixSteps.title: Inspect intake
fixSteps.instruction: Check boot and vacuum lines for leaks.

fixSteps.title: Clean MAF
fixSteps.instruction: Use MAF-safe cleaner on the sensor element.

fixSteps.title: Test throttle body
fixSteps.instruction: Check TPS sweep and throttle plate operation.

faq.a: Short term, but vacuum leaks can damage the engine long term.

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 2 Range/Performance
shortDescription: Secondary intake air temperature sensor reading out of expected range.
fullDescription:
P0096 is set when the PCM finds the IAT2 sensor output implausible compared to other temperature sensors at start-up and running conditions.

Common on turbocharged engines where IAT2 measures post-intercooler temperature.
safetyImpact: Minor; boost and fuel trims may be slightly off.

fixSteps.title: Compare temps
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool to compare IAT1 and IAT2 after cold soak.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new IAT2 if readings are off.

faq.a: Often in the charge pipe after the intercooler.

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Low
shortDescription: IAT2 sensor reading below minimum threshold.
fullDescription:
P0097 indicates IAT2 voltage is abnormally low, suggesting a short to ground or a failed sensor stuck at high temperature reading.

The PCM may use a default value during diagnosis.

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit High
fullDescription:
P0098 shows IAT2 voltage is higher than expected, usually from an open circuit or disconnected sensor.

Repair by checking connector and replacing sensor if needed.

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 2 Intermittent
shortDescription: IAT2 sensor signal drops out intermittently.
fullDescription:
P0099 is stored when the IAT2 signal becomes erratic or drops briefly. Often caused by loose connectors or damaged wiring.

Intermittent faults are easiest to find by wiggle-testing while monitoring data.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test
fixSteps.instruction: Move harness while watching live data.

faq.q: Why is it hard to find?
faq.a: Fault only occurs under specific conditions.

title: HO2S Circuit Slow Response Bank 2 Sensor 2
shortDescription: Downstream oxygen sensor switches too slowly on bank 2.
fullDescription:
P0159 indicates bank 2 sensor 2 is not responding to mixture changes as quickly as expected. Aging or contaminated sensors lose response speed.

Replacement typically restores proper switching rate and catalyst monitoring.

fixSteps.title: Check for exhaust leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect pipes ahead of the sensor.

title: HO2S Circuit No Activity Bank 2 Sensor 3
shortDescription: No signal activity from bank 2 sensor 3.
fullDescription:
P0160 indicates the PCM is not seeing any switching activity from bank 2 sensor 3. Usually caused by sensor failure, wiring, or cold sensor that never heats.

Verify heater function first if P0061-P0064 are also stored.

faq.a: Only some applications have a third sensor.

title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: Flex-fuel composition sensor signal is intermittent.
fullDescription:
P0184 is set on flex-fuel vehicles when the ethanol composition sensor signal becomes intermittent. Wiring or sensor is typically at fault.

The PCM uses this data to adjust fueling between gasoline and E85.
safetyImpact: Rough running possible with wrong fuel blend.

faq.a: Yes, on default values, but may be rough on E85.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit
shortDescription: Fault on secondary fuel temperature sensor circuit.
fullDescription:
P0185 indicates an electrical fault in the fuel temperature sensor B circuit. Fuel temperature affects density and therefore injection compensation.

Diesel and flex-fuel vehicles commonly use this sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new fuel temp sensor B.

faq.a: Usually on the fuel rail or return line.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Range/Performance
shortDescription: Fuel temperature B reading is implausible.
fullDescription:
P0186 is stored when the fuel temp sensor B shows a value that doesn't match expected conditions. Could be a stuck sensor or wiring issue.

Compare with ambient and coolant temperature at cold start.

fixSteps.title: Compare temps
fixSteps.instruction: Check against ambient and coolant temps cold.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Install new fuel temp B sensor.

faq.a: Not urgent, but fix before emissions testing.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
shortDescription: Fuel temp B signal voltage too low.
fullDescription:
P0187 indicates signal voltage below minimum threshold on fuel temperature sensor B. Typically a short to ground or sensor internal short.

Diagnose by disconnecting and testing resistance.

faq.a: Usually yes, due to NTC thermistor behavior.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
shortDescription: Fuel temp B signal voltage too high.
fullDescription:
P0188 indicates signal voltage above maximum threshold, usually from an open circuit.

Check connector and wiring first.

faq.q: Can this set at cold start?
faq.a: Yes, if sensor is open circuit.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Intermittent
shortDescription: Fuel temp B signal drops out intermittently.
fullDescription:
P0189 is set when the fuel temp B sensor signal becomes erratic. Typically wiring or a failing sensor.

Wiggle-test the harness while monitoring live data to locate the fault.

title: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: Secondary fuel pump circuit is intermittent.
fullDescription:
P0233 is stored when the PCM sees intermittent activity on the secondary fuel pump circuit. Common on twin-pump systems.

Check relay, wiring, and pump performance.
safetyImpact: Fuel starvation under load is possible.

faq.a: A booster or auxiliary pump used under high demand.

title: Turbocharger Overboost Condition
shortDescription: Turbocharger boost pressure exceeded safe limit.
fullDescription:
P0234 indicates the PCM saw boost pressure above the maximum allowed. A stuck wastegate, failed BPS, or tuner modifications are typical causes.

Driving with overboost can damage the engine and turbo.

faq.a: Only to a shop; avoid high boost.

title: Turbocharger Boost Sensor A Circuit
shortDescription: Fault in boost pressure sensor A circuit.
fullDescription:
P0235 indicates an electrical fault in the boost pressure sensor circuit. The PCM uses this sensor to manage boost via wastegate or VGT control.

Wiring and sensor replacement are common fixes.

faq.a: On turbo vehicles, often a dedicated BPS.

title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B
shortDescription: Diesel injection pump metering control B fault.
fullDescription:
P0254 is a diesel-specific code indicating a fault in the secondary fuel metering control on the injection pump.

Causes include pump control solenoid failure or wiring.
safetyImpact: Loss of power and potential no-start.

faq.a: Yes, addresses fuel metering on diesels.

title: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit Low-advanced
shortDescription: Cylinder 1 injector control circuit voltage low.
fullDescription:
P0261 indicates low voltage on the cylinder 1 injector control circuit, usually a short to ground or failed injector.

The affected cylinder misfires or does not fire at all.

faq.a: Varies by engine; consult service manual.

title: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit High-advanced
shortDescription: Cylinder 1 injector control circuit voltage high.
fullDescription:
P0262 indicates high voltage on the cyl 1 injector circuit, typically from an open circuit or short to battery.

Check connector and wiring first.

faq.a: Yes, to confirm the fault follows the injector.

title: Cylinder 1 Contribution/Balance
shortDescription: Cylinder 1 producing less power than expected.
fullDescription:
P0263 is set when cylinder 1 fails the contribution test. Causes include low compression, weak injector, or ignition problem.

The PCM evaluates crankshaft acceleration per cylinder.

fixSteps.title: Inspect spark and injector
fixSteps.instruction: Swap coil and injector to isolate.

faq.a: PCM measures each cylinder's impact on RPM.

title: Cylinder 2 Injector Circuit Low-advanced
fullDescription:
P0264 indicates low voltage on cylinder 2 injector control circuit. Same diagnostic approach as other cylinder-specific injector codes.

Start with injector resistance measurement.

title: Cylinder 2 Injector Circuit High-advanced
fullDescription: P0265 indicates an open or short-to-power on the cyl 2 injector circuit. Inspect wiring first.

title: Cylinder 2 Contribution/Balance
shortDescription: Cyl 2 low contribution to engine output.
fullDescription: P0266 indicates cylinder 2 is producing less power than expected. Compression, fuel, or ignition issues.

faq.a: Uneven crankshaft speed at cyl 2 TDC.

title: Cylinder 3 Injector Circuit Low-advanced
fullDescription: P0267 is low voltage on cyl 3 injector control circuit.

title: Cylinder 3 Injector Circuit High-advanced
fullDescription: P0268 is high voltage on cyl 3 injector circuit, typical open or short to battery.

title: Cylinder 3 Contribution/Balance
fullDescription: P0269 indicates cylinder 3 contribution is below threshold. Diagnose with compression and injector tests.

title: Cylinder 4 Injector Circuit Low-advanced
fullDescription: P0270 is low voltage on cyl 4 injector circuit.

title: Cylinder 11 Injector Circuit Low
fullDescription: P0289 is low voltage on cyl 11 injector on V10/V12 engines.

title: Cylinder 11 Injector Circuit High
fullDescription: P0290 is an open or short to battery on cyl 11 injector circuit.

faq.a: Often yes; intake removal may be needed.

title: Cylinder 11 Contribution/Balance
fullDescription: P0291 indicates cyl 11 is producing less power than expected.

title: Cylinder 12 Injector Circuit Low
fullDescription: P0292 is a short to ground on cyl 12 injector circuit.

title: Cylinder 12 Injector Circuit High
fullDescription: P0293 is open or short to battery on cyl 12 injector.

title: Cylinder 12 Contribution/Balance
fullDescription: P0294 indicates cyl 12 produces less power than expected.

title: Turbocharger Underboost Condition
fullDescription:
P0299 is set when boost pressure is lower than commanded. Common causes include boost leaks, stuck wastegate, or worn turbo.

Check all charge pipes and couplers.
safetyImpact: Reduced power; can enter limp mode.

faq.a: A blown intercooler hose or clamp.

title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected (freeze frame detailed)
shortDescription: Detailed cylinder 1 misfire with freeze frame analysis.
fullDescription:
P0301 indicates misfires detected on cylinder 1. Advanced diagnosis involves examining freeze frame data to correlate misfire with RPM, load, and temperature.

Review short/long-term fuel trims and ignition dwell at the moment of misfire.
safetyImpact: Catalyst damage risk; avoid hard driving.

fixSteps.title: Swap coil/plug
fixSteps.instruction: Move cyl 1 coil to cyl 2; see if misfire follows.

fixSteps.title: Fuel and compression check
fixSteps.instruction: If hardware OK, test fuel and compression.

faq.a: Snapshot of data when code was set.

title: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected (detailed)
shortDescription: Advanced cyl 2 misfire diagnosis with load analysis.
fullDescription: P0302 advanced workup involves checking cyl 2 ignition, fuel, and compression under matching conditions from freeze frame.

title: Cylinder 3 Misfire Detected (detailed)
fullDescription: Detailed diagnosis of cyl 3 misfire. Review all inputs including fuel trims and knock sensor data.

title: Cylinder 4 Misfire Detected (detailed)
fullDescription: Cyl 4 misfire with detailed root cause analysis.

title: Cylinder 5 Misfire Detected (detailed)
fullDescription: Detailed diagnosis for cyl 5 misfire on V6/V8/V10/V12 engines.

title: Cylinder 6 Misfire Detected (detailed)
fullDescription: Detailed workup for cyl 6 misfire.

title: Cylinder 7 Misfire Detected (detailed)
fullDescription: Cyl 7 misfire with detailed diagnosis.

title: Cylinder 8 Misfire Detected (detailed)
fullDescription: Cyl 8 misfire detailed analysis.

title: Cylinder 9 Misfire Detected (detailed)
fullDescription: Cyl 9 misfire on V10/V12 engines.

title: Cylinder 10 Misfire Detected (detailed)
fullDescription: Cyl 10 misfire detailed analysis.

faq.a: V10s like BMW S85, Audi R8.

title: Cylinder 11 Misfire Detected (detailed)
fullDescription: Cyl 11 misfire in V12 engines.

title: Cylinder 12 Misfire Detected (detailed)
fullDescription: Cyl 12 misfire in V12 engines.

title: EGR Insufficient Flow Detected
shortDescription: EGR system not flowing enough exhaust gas.
fullDescription:
P0401 is set when EGR flow is lower than commanded. Carbon buildup, stuck valve, or blocked passages are common.

Cleaning or replacing the EGR valve often resolves it.

title: EGR Excessive Flow Detected
fullDescription:
P0402 indicates EGR flow is higher than expected, typically from a stuck-open valve or failed DPFE sensor.

Stuck-open EGR causes rough idle and stalling.

title: EGR Control Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: Electrical fault in EGR control circuit.
fullDescription: P0403 indicates an electrical issue in the EGR control circuit. Wiring or solenoid/stepper motor failure.

faq.a: Yes, it helps reduce NOx and improve efficiency.

title: EGR Control Circuit Range/Performance
shortDescription: EGR position does not match command.
fullDescription: P0404 is set when the EGR position sensor does not report expected values for the commanded position.

fixSteps.title: Replace EGR
fixSteps.instruction: If cleaning fails, install new unit.

faq.a: Any carb or throttle body cleaner.

title: EGR Sensor A Circuit Low
shortDescription: EGR position sensor A voltage too low.
fullDescription: P0405 indicates low voltage on EGR position sensor A, usually short to ground or failed sensor.

title: EGR Sensor A Circuit High
shortDescription: EGR position sensor A voltage too high.
fullDescription: P0406 is set when position sensor voltage is above threshold, typically open circuit.

title: EGR Sensor B Circuit Low
shortDescription: EGR sensor B voltage too low.
fullDescription: P0407 indicates low voltage on a secondary EGR position sensor.

faq.a: Some EGR systems use dual sensors.

title: EGR Sensor B Circuit High
shortDescription: EGR sensor B voltage too high.
fullDescription: P0408 is set when sensor B voltage exceeds threshold.

title: EGR Sensor A Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: General malfunction in EGR sensor A circuit.
fullDescription: P0409 indicates a general electrical fault in the EGR sensor A circuit.

title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve B Malfunction
fullDescription:
P0415 indicates a malfunction in the secondary air injection switching valve B. The SAI system injects air into exhaust at cold start to help catalyst light-off.

Corroded valves or weak pumps are common.

title: Secondary Air Injection Relay A Control Circuit
shortDescription: Fault in SAI relay A control.
fullDescription: P0418 indicates an electrical fault in the secondary air injection relay A control circuit.

title: Secondary Air Injection Relay B Control Circuit
shortDescription: Fault in SAI relay B control.
fullDescription: P0419 is similar to P0418 but for the secondary relay.

title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor Malfunction
fullDescription: P0450 indicates a generic malfunction in the EVAP pressure (FTP) sensor.

title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit
shortDescription: Fault in fuel level sensor A circuit.
fullDescription: P0460 indicates a malfunction in the fuel level sensor circuit used by the PCM for EVAP diagnostics.

faq.a: Drop fuel tank or under rear seat.

title: Fuel Level Sensor A Range/Performance
shortDescription: Fuel level sensor A reading implausible.
fullDescription: P0461 indicates the fuel level sender is reporting a value inconsistent with usage rate.

title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Low
shortDescription: Fuel level sensor A voltage too low.
fullDescription: P0462 indicates low voltage from the fuel level sender circuit.

title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit High
shortDescription: Fuel level sensor A voltage too high.
fullDescription: P0463 indicates high voltage from fuel level sender, often open circuit.

title: Fuel Level Sensor A Intermittent
fullDescription: P0464 indicates the fuel level signal is erratic.

title: Turbocharger Wastegate Solenoid A Malfunction
shortDescription: Fault in turbo wastegate solenoid A.
fullDescription: P0243 indicates an electrical fault in the wastegate control solenoid. Controls boost pressure.

title: Turbocharger Wastegate Solenoid A Range/Performance
shortDescription: Wastegate solenoid A performance out of spec.
fullDescription: P0244 is set when solenoid response doesn't match commanded duty cycle.

title: Turbocharger Wastegate Solenoid A Low
fullDescription: P0245 indicates short to ground or low voltage on wastegate solenoid A.

title: Turbocharger Wastegate Solenoid A High
fullDescription: P0246 indicates open circuit or short to battery on wastegate solenoid A.

title: Transmission Control System Electrical
fullDescription: P0702 indicates a general electrical malfunction in the transmission control system. Often wiring or ground issues.

faq.a: Varies; sometimes on top of transmission.

title: Brake Switch B Circuit Malfunction
fullDescription: P0703 indicates a fault in the brake switch B circuit used by the transmission for TCC release.
safetyImpact: Cruise control disabled, possible shift issues.

title: Transmission Range Sensor Circuit High
shortDescription: Transmission range sensor voltage too high.
fullDescription: P0708 indicates the TRS (neutral safety switch) voltage is above threshold, often misaligned or failed switch.

title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
fullDescription: P0711 indicates the transmission fluid temperature sensor is reading inconsistent with operating conditions.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new TFT; may require pan drop.

faq.a: Good practice when pan is dropped.

title: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor Circuit
fullDescription: P0715 indicates a fault in the turbine/input speed sensor circuit used to monitor transmission input shaft speed.

title: Input Speed Sensor Range/Performance
fullDescription: P0716 indicates the input speed sensor signal is not consistent with other engine/trans data.

title: Input Speed Sensor No Signal
shortDescription: No signal from input speed sensor.
fullDescription: P0717 indicates no signal from ISS, typically open circuit or dead sensor.

title: Input Speed Sensor Intermittent
fullDescription: P0718 indicates ISS signal drops out intermittently.

title: Brake Switch B Circuit Low
fullDescription: P0719 indicates low voltage on brake switch B, often short to ground.

title: Engine Speed Input Circuit No Signal
shortDescription: TCM not seeing engine RPM input.
fullDescription: P0727 indicates the TCM is not receiving engine speed data. Usually CAN bus or wiring issue.

title: Gear 1 Incorrect Ratio
fullDescription: P0731 is set when input/output speed ratio in 1st gear doesn't match expected value. Indicates slip or internal transmission problem.

title: Gear 2 Incorrect Ratio
fullDescription: P0732 indicates incorrect 2nd gear ratio.

title: Gear 3 Incorrect Ratio
fullDescription: P0733 indicates incorrect 3rd gear ratio.

title: Gear 4 Incorrect Ratio
fullDescription: P0734 indicates incorrect 4th gear ratio.

title: Gear 5 Incorrect Ratio
fullDescription: P0735 indicates incorrect 5th gear ratio.

faq.a: Applies to any trans with 5+ gears.

title: Reverse Gear Incorrect Ratio
fullDescription: P0736 indicates reverse gear ratio is not as expected.

title: TCM Engine Speed Output Circuit
fullDescription: P0737 indicates the TCM engine speed output circuit has a fault.

title: TCM Engine Speed Output Circuit Low
fullDescription: P0738 indicates low voltage on TCM engine speed output.

title: TCC Circuit Performance/Stuck Off (detailed)
fullDescription:
P0741 advanced diagnosis: TCC not locking up as commanded. Check solenoid resistance, valve body, and fluid condition.

Dirty fluid commonly causes TCC solenoid sticking.

faq.a: Yes, always try fluid service first.

title: TCC Circuit Stuck On
fullDescription: P0742 indicates TCC is locked when it should be released, causing stalling when coming to a stop.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Electrical
shortDescription: Electrical fault in pressure control solenoid A.
fullDescription: P0748 indicates an electrical fault in the transmission pressure control solenoid A circuit.

title: Starter Relay Circuit
shortDescription: Fault in starter relay control circuit.
fullDescription: P0615 indicates an electrical fault in the starter relay circuit controlled by the PCM.

title: Starter Relay Circuit Low
fullDescription: P0616 indicates short to ground in starter relay circuit.

title: Starter Relay Circuit High
fullDescription: P0617 indicates open circuit in starter relay control.

title: Alternative Fuel Control Module KAM Error
shortDescription: Alt fuel module keep-alive memory error.
fullDescription: P0618 indicates a keep-alive memory fault in the alternative fuel control module (CNG/LPG/flex vehicles).

title: Immobilizer Lamp Control Circuit
fullDescription: P0648 indicates a fault in the immobilizer indicator lamp control circuit.

title: Speed Control Lamp Output Circuit
fullDescription: P0649 indicates an issue with the speed control (cruise) indicator lamp output.

title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit Bank 1
fullDescription: P0660 indicates an electrical fault in the intake manifold tuning valve control circuit on bank 1.

title: IMTV Control Circuit Low Bank 1
fullDescription: P0661 indicates short to ground in IMTV bank 1 circuit.

title: IMTV Control Circuit High Bank 1
fullDescription: P0662 indicates open circuit in IMTV bank 1 control.

title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Circuit
fullDescription: P0671 indicates an electrical fault on cylinder 1 glow plug circuit (diesel).

faq.a: Often wise to do as a set.

title: Cylinder 2 Glow Plug Circuit
fullDescription: P0672 indicates cyl 2 glow plug fault.

title: Cylinder 3 Glow Plug Circuit
fullDescription: P0673 indicates cyl 3 glow plug fault.

title: Cylinder 4 Glow Plug Circuit
fullDescription: P0674 indicates cyl 4 glow plug fault.

title: Cylinder 5 Glow Plug Circuit
fullDescription: P0675 indicates cyl 5 glow plug fault.

title: Cylinder 6 Glow Plug Circuit
fullDescription: P0676 indicates cyl 6 glow plug fault.

title: Cylinder 7 Glow Plug Circuit
fullDescription: P0677 indicates cyl 7 glow plug fault on V8 diesels.

title: Cylinder 8 Glow Plug Circuit
fullDescription: P0678 indicates cyl 8 glow plug fault on V8 diesels.

faq.a: Usually recommended if several have failed.
